subject: mathematics
title: Fractions: Equal Parts of a Whole
summary: A fraction represents one or more equal parts of a whole—whether a pizza, an energy bar, or a collection of objects.
visualInteractiveHint: Adjust the numerator (top) and denominator (bottom). Compare the circular pizza and rectangular bar to see how both show the exact same share.
workedExampleTitle: Why do 1/4 and 2/8 represent the exact same amount?

workedSteps.title: Step 1: The denominator demands equal parts
workedSteps.explanation: Cut a pizza or bar into 4 equal pieces and take 1 piece: you have 1/4 ("one fourth").

workedSteps.title: Step 2: Split each fourth in half
workedSteps.explanation: If we slice each of the 4 pieces into 2 equal parts, there are now 8 smaller slices, and our share covers 2 of those 8.

workedSteps.title: Step 3: Adding fractions of the same size
workedSteps.explanation: To add 1/4 + 2/4, add the numerators (1 + 2 = 3) and keep the denominator 4 because the slice size did not change.

whyItWorks: Multiplying or dividing top and bottom by the same number is multiplying by 1: it changes the slice count without changing the total shaded amount.

commonMistake.wrongExample: Common trap: computing 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/8 by adding the denominators too.
commonMistake.correction: The denominator names the size of the piece ("fourths"). 1 fourth plus 2 fourths equals 3 fourths (3/4), not 3 eighths!

deepDiveExtra: The larger the denominator, the smaller each individual slice becomes: 1/8 of a bar is half the size of 1/4 of a bar.

quickChecks.question: Which of these fractions is equivalent to 1/2?
quickChecks.explanation: 3 is half of 6, so 3/6 simplifies directly to 1/2.
